Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The MyONECI+ app (launched April 2025) enables digital identity authentication using PKI, encrypted certificates, NFC and biometric authentication from smartphones. Identity Verification Terminals (TVIs, deployed from 2022) allow offline authentication via chip reading and biometrics. The VERIF app from ONECI is used in the e-Justice platform. The identite.ci portal provides digital identity services with ONECI's visible electronic seal (CEV).

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The ONECI VERIF application is integrated into the e-Justice platform (launched January 2025) for identity authentication. The E-Administrative Procedures platform (105 digitized services) is operational. The identite.ci portal allows access to government identity services. Citizens can generate official documents online with ONECI's electronic seal (CEV).

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: The MyONECI+ app (April 2025) allows individuals to access their identity document and data on their smartphones, based on the RNPP. The identite.ci application also allows access to dematerialized identity documents. Law No. 2013-450 grants individuals the right to obtain their personal data in an understandable form.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The CNI is the primary document for KYC in Cote d'Ivoire. BCEAO and CENTIF-CI mandate KYC for all financial services using CNI or passport. API-based real-time CNI lookups via ONECI's database are available for banks and fintechs. The country is a GIABA member aligned with FATF standards. Law No. 2016-992 mandates KYC across regulated entities.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Courts of First Instance issue the Certificate of Nationality, which is required as a base document for the CNI. Courts also issue supplementary judgments to replace lost birth records. The e-Justice platform (launched January 2025) integrates ONECI's VERIF authentication for judicial services. Courts thus play a structural role in identity governance.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: ONECI manages both civil registration and identification. A birth certificate is a required base document for the CNI. CRVS digitization is underway (pilot in Grand-Bassam 2024, 200,000 records), and ONECI is expanding to 250+ civil status centers. The RNPP links civil registration data with biometric ID. However, national CRVS digitization is not yet complete.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law No. 2013-450 establishes rules on interconnection of personal data (must not discriminate, must use security measures, must be proportionate). Prior notification or ARTCI authorization is required for data processing. Cross-border data transfers only permitted to countries with equivalent protection. However, operational rules specific to ID data sharing are not yet fully codified.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: The biometric national ID card is regulated through a specific law mandating compulsory biometric enrollment for all Ivorians 16+, with NIN assigned at birth via the RNPP. However, there is no single standalone digital identity law covering the full digital ID lifecycle. The legal mandate derives from older NIC laws and specific decrees.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on the Protection of Personal Data is in force, governing collection, processing, storage, and transfer of personal data. It is an adaptation of the ECOWAS Supplementary Act on Personal Data Protection (2010) and provides rights to access, correction, and erasure, as well as requiring consent for sensitive data including biometrics.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: ARTCI (Autorité de Régulation des Télécommunications/TIC de Côte d'Ivoire) is the independent DPA with powers to receive complaints, conduct audits, impose administrative penalties (up to CFA10M), grant authorizations for sensitive data processing including biometrics, and maintain a public register of data processing operations. It has actively issued press releases and enforcement warnings (e.g., June 2024 biometrics in workplaces).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNI (Carte Nationale d'Identite) is the primary legal proof of identity in Cote d'Ivoire, required for government services, financial transactions, voting, and accessing social services. The ONECI-issued digital identity (via MyONECI+ and identite.ci) also provides legally certified documents with ONECI's visible electronic seal (CEV).

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A dedicated legal framework exists: Law 62-64 (1962 NIC), Ordinance 2007-06 on NIC conditions, Decree 2001-103 (ONECI creation), laws 2002-03 and 2004-303 on identification, plus the law establishing the compulsory biometric ID card for all Ivorians 16+. Law No. 2013-450 on personal data protection provides comprehensive data rights governance.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: ONECI (Office National de l'Etat Civil et de l'Identification), under the Ministry of Interior and Security, is the national body responsible for civil registration and identification. It manages the CNI register, RNPP, and oversees the technical partnership with Semlex for card production.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalization oversees digital transformation including ONECI activities, with a budget of CFA60.78 billion ($96.8M) in 2025 and CFA83.2 billion ($145.9M) in 2026. ONECI falls under the Ministry of Interior and Security. While not direct Ministry of Finance oversight of the ID system, budgetary oversight exists through the National Assembly and relevant ministries.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The ID system has a mixed sustainability model: applicants pay 5000 FCFA per card (generating revenue through a PPP with Semlex for 36M cards over 12 years, valued at 460 billion FCFA total). World Bank WURI programme provided €1.8M to support ID reform. State budget includes ID digitization. Fee revenue partially offsets costs, but dependency on Semlex PPP raises vendor lock-in concerns.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The CNI biometric enrollment collects all 10 fingerprints and a facial photograph, with AFIS deduplication (Safran Morpho). The CNAM health insurance card also collects 10 fingerprints and face photo. Biometric residence cards for foreigners collect fingerprints and facial images.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The CNI register is electronic (initially 6.38 million records, now 14M+ NNIs issued). The RNPP is being built as a central electronic national population register. CRVS digitisation is underway via a pilot in Grand-Bassam (April 2024, 200,000 records digitized). Civil registration is still largely paper-based nationally but transitioning.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Cote d'Ivoire operates a biometric national identity card (CNI) issued by ONECI, backed by the National Register of Physical Persons (RNPP). The MyONECI+ app (launched April 2025) provides digital ID access via smartphone using PKI, NFC and biometric authentication. Over 14 million NNIs issued by 2024.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The identification ecosystem remains fragmented: the CNI register, CNAM health insurance database, and electoral register are decoupled. The RNPP (National Register of Physical Persons) is being built to serve as a federation hub. ONECI joined the OSIA initiative (Secure Identity Alliance) to support open standards for interoperability. The WURI programme (World Bank) supports interoperability with ECOWAS states.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNI is required for opening bank accounts, mobile money accounts, and accessing financial services, as mandated by BCEAO and CENTIF-CI regulations. Cote d'Ivoire leads UEMOA in digital payments with 45% mobile money penetration and 17.5M internet users. Identity verification via ONECI database is used in digital onboarding by banks and fintechs.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The biometric national ID card costs 5000 FCFA (~$8.40) for the card itself, plus estimated 10,000-13,000 FCFA ($17-20 total) for supporting documents and transportation. This is a significant barrier for many Ivorians, as 46% live below the poverty line. Civil society groups have campaigned against this fee as exclusionary. The initial 2009 issuance was free.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Cote d'Ivoire is a founding member (Phase 1, 2018) of the World Bank WURI programme, which aims for cross-border mutual recognition of foundational ID systems across ECOWAS states. The country is working toward ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC) compliance. ECOWAS is adopting a single biometric identity card for free movement. MyONECI+ certificates carry electronic seals valid internationally.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The CNI is mandatory for all Ivorians 16 and above. National identity certificates can be issued to children aged 5-15. Babies are assigned a National Identification Number (NIN) at birth via the RNPP. Thus the system covers all ages, from birth (NIN), with a formal card from age 5.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The biometric national ID card is compulsory for all Ivorian citizens aged 16 and above. The president announced the card would become mandatory for all adults 16+. Civil registration (birth) is also legally mandatory since 1964, though compliance is incomplete. The UHC health insurance enrollment is also mandatory.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The CNAM (universal health coverage, CMU) requires biometric enrollment and ID verification for coverage. As of 2024, mobile enrollment centers have been deployed to expand reach. ~40% of the population was enrolled in CMU by 2024. The CMU identifier is being aligned with the national ID number. Healthcare providers use ID for beneficiary identification.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Foreign nationals legally resident in Cote d'Ivoire are eligible for a biometric Carte de Resident (residence card) issued by ONECI, which stores fingerprints and facial images. Approximately 500,000 resident alien cards had been issued as of the 2016 World Bank diagnostic. New biometric residence cards were introduced for foreign workers in 2025.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: By 2024, over 14 million NNIs (National Identification Numbers) have been issued, and approximately 80%+ of adults are covered by biometric ID. A 2024 KYC guide cites over 14M biometric ID cards issued covering over 80% of adults. Earlier data showed 64% of eligible adults (16+) in 2016; coverage has grown significantly with the 2020-2022 enrollment drive. Total population ~32.7M; ~55-60% total population covered.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Cote d'Ivoire has Decree No. 2021-916 adopting the General Information Systems Security Reference Framework (RGSSI) and Critical Infrastructure Protection Plan (PPIC). ARTCI conducts audits of data processing operations. The ITU 2024 Global Cybersecurity Index places Cote d'Ivoire at Tier 3/5 with strong legislative and organisational frameworks. CI-CERT (Computer Emergency Response Team) is operational. Regular security monitoring is required for essential services operators.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration with valid ID has been mandatory since 2011, tightened in March 2017 to require registration only at operator outlets. Unregistered SIMs are blocked after deadlines. Children under 16 cannot buy SIMs without a legal guardian. ARTCI enforces identity requirements for SIM activation. All major operators (Orange, MTN, Moov) comply.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The CNI is required to access government social services. The World Bank social protection project uses identity for beneficiary verification. The CMU health insurance program requires ID for enrollment. The social register (Registre Social Unifie) uses ID to verify eligibility for social transfers. The World Bank-supported cash transfer program disbursed payments to 100,000+ new beneficiary households in 2023.
